one_line: A human-readable brand portal that exposes page- and session-aware brand guidance as WebMCP tools for agents.
what_it_does: Presents an editorial brand book and lets a compatible agent retrieve active-page guidance, prepare brand-constrained copy or image-prompt packages, and stage the result back into a visible Studio review state with sources, changes, rules, rationale, warnings, and human controls.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central rather than decorative: route-specific tools expose structured brand context without DOM scraping, and preparation/staging returns work into the same session for human review. A general UI-driving agent could approximate the workflow, but with materially more fragile extraction, context loss, and state handling.
leverage_evidence: About text describes exactly nine page- and session-aware browser Site Tools registered with document.modelContext.registerTool().
The described flow retrieves active-page guidance, prepares a structured brief, and stages the result back into the portal; frames show a prepared session and bounded next affordance.
The frame sheet includes the active-page → Site Tools → AI tools model and emphasizes avoiding lossy prompt reconstruction.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentionally scoped static application with a complete claimed copy journey and visible review/audit states. Contact-sheet frames show the Studio workflow, named agent interaction, bounded session, and material-change review. However, there is no transcript or independently observed live run, so end-to-end completion is claimed rather than demonstrated directly.
execution_evidence: FACTS report an alive demo link and ten working direct routes, plus automated graph, schema, browser, accessibility, and unit checks.
Frames show 'Prepare Wonderland copy for review,' 'Speak with Cheshire Cat,' a prepared session, agent activity surface, and 'Every material change stays visible' review screens.
About text explicitly limits the image workflow to a generator-neutral prompt package and states that tools do not approve or publish.
impact_rationale: The product addresses a concrete problem for marketing teams and external agencies: faithfully applying brand guidance to AI-assisted copy and visual prompting while retaining human responsibility. The proposed traceability and review controls are credible and useful, though the packet does not provide measured task-time or error-reduction outcomes.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies marketing workers and suppliers who currently copy and interpret brand portals into prompts.
The claimed Studio output includes original source, proposed draft, material changes, applied rules, rationale, warnings, and edit/keep/discard/reset controls.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows brand-copy rewriting with guidance such as 'Clear before clever,' a change summary, and why-it-changed notes.
creativity_rationale: The fresh concept is treating a brand portal's active page as executable, context-dependent agent capability while preserving the portal as a human-facing editorial artifact. The combination of page-aware affordances, bounded sessions, staged outputs, and explicit acknowledgement of lossy interpretation is a notably original interaction model for the challenge.
creativity_evidence: About text frames WebMCP as changing brand rules from static text into executable, page-contextual affordances.
The visual narrative contrasts portal guidance, human interpretation, reconstructed prompts, and 'Lossy,' then presents active page → Site Tools → AI tools without removing the human.
The project pursues the idea across both language and visual prompt preparation rather than only exposing a generic button.
usability_note: The editorial portal, bounded next affordances, named agent, visible change review, and ordinary human controls suggest a clear workflow; compatibility is limited to WebMCP-enabled hosts and the packet lacks direct hands-on verification.
red_flags: No public repository and no video transcript; technical claims are primarily self-reported.
The frame sheets show product states and an agent/activity surface but do not clearly expose complete native tool-call details at readable resolution.
No quantitative evaluation is provided, and the image journey is described as prompt packaging rather than image generation.
standouts: Strong human/agent shared-state model with route- and session-aware WebMCP affordances.
Excellent provenance and review framing: source, diffs, rules, rationale, and warnings remain visible.
Clear scope honesty: proposes and stages work but does not claim approval, publication, or generated imagery.
advance_reason: Advance: the project offers a strong, distinctive WebMCP-centered workflow with credible impact and substantial visual evidence of a coherent product; remaining uncertainty is mainly lack of independently observed end-to-end execution.
